title: Replace heuristic test execution with explicit project validation adapters
files: scripts/factory/{test-changed,test-full,verify}.ps1; scripts/lib.ps1; templates/factory.config.yaml; workflows/{implement,fix-review}.yaml; tests/fixtures/*/scripts/factory/; tests/run-tests.ps1; docs/project-integration.md
objective: Execute the project's existing configured validation adapters exactly once and produce isolated, trustworthy receipts.
decisions: Reuse validation.changed/full/verify scalars and Read-FactoryConfig; do not add a parallel config file or infer test runners by extension.

Resolve project root from the current worktree Git root; config is .ai/factory/factory.config.yaml. Execute the explicitly configured command through documented pwsh subprocess semantics from that root. Missing config/command, same-wrapper recursion or unsupported config are errors, not discovery fallbacks.

Replace shared wrappers with a common dispatcher plus thin stage entry points. Include verify in required full verification, and fix project-path handling in verify rather than checking the shared runtime for a project pin.

Store logs/receipt in worktree-local .factory/artifacts/validation/<stage>/<attempt-guid>/; a concise stable pointer can exist within that worktree only. Bind receipts to repository/head SHA, stage, command, start/end, exitCode, artifact paths and status; dirty-tree evidence cannot authorize head-only merge checks.

Missing/empty validation cannot count as passed. Explicitly unsupported optional targeted coverage may report skipped, but full/verify required stages fail closed. Preserve project adapter semantics; wrappers report command success, not invented test counts.
steps: Add fixture commands and a shared dispatcher that loads existing config, validates stage and starts a child process with separate bounded stdout/stderr.
Replace test discovery loops and shared artifact paths; make exceptions/failed launch/nonzero exit agree with receipt and wrapper exit.
Wire existing workflow command steps to stage adapters and require full+verify for review, preserving already-resolved no-op behavior.
Update project integration/migration guidance and fixture adapters; cover supported PS/.NET/JS/Godot via stub command adapters instead of installing all runtimes in tests.
criteria: Configured changed/full/verify commands run exactly once from the correct worktree; no source/test-file enumeration occurs.
Empty project, missing command, recursion, setup exception and nonzero child exit produce explicit non-passing evidence and nonzero required-stage exit.
Two parallel worktrees/attempts never share result paths or write to the mounted runtime.
Both full and verify requirements are enforced; already-resolved issues still no-op.
Paths with spaces and Windows/Linux command semantics are covered by subprocess tests.
tests: Fixture subprocess tests with counters/exit injection, cwd assertions, dirty/head identity, concurrent attempts and bounded log output; full Factory suite on Windows/Linux.
scope: No GitHub merge routing, model changes, automatic project discovery or package-specific test heuristics.

title: Retry incomplete Factory reconciliation when the deployed SHA is unchanged
files: scripts/deploy/factory-autodeploy.sh; scripts/sync-all-automations.ps1; integrations/bazzite/factory-autodeploy.{service,timer}; tests/ (stubbed autodeploy harness); docs/shared-factory.md
objective: Retry failed parity/reconciliation independently of whether the checkout advanced, and record success only after full convergence.
decisions: Remove unchanged-SHA success shortcut. On every timer invocation, retain flock and dirty/divergence checks, fetch the explicit deploy ref, and ensure fast-forward before parity/sync.

Compare host SHA and container-visible SHA plus hashes of workflow-referenced scripts/catalog and VERSION, so equal VERSION or equal Git metadata alone cannot hide a wrong mount/stale files. Use only registered paths; do not discover a replacement checkout.

Run idempotent sync-all on every healthy tick, including unchanged SHA; this is the explicit drift-reconciliation policy and avoids false success after registry changes or out-of-band automation edits.

Write success receipt atomically only after all configured targets succeed, containing sourceSha, version, registryDigest, parity result and target receipts. Store it in an ignored host-local state path, not a tracked checkout file.

A failed attempt keeps last successful receipt but emits a distinct failure receipt; next normal tick retries. --force stays backward compatible but is no longer required for recovery. Do not add reset/clean/stash.
steps: Build shell harness with temporary remote and fake podman/sync/clock commands; reproduce advance-then-fail followed by unchanged tick.
Refactor reconciliation policy and same-version content parity, preserve documented blocked exit codes where possible and document any new code.
Emit atomic success/failure receipts with registry snapshot digest; preserve global non-overlap lock.
Cover already-current/drift, missing registry, mixed target failure, container outage, process interruption, dirty/diverged checkout and lock contention.
criteria: One-time failure after advancement recovers on the next ordinary tick without --force or another commit.
An unchanged successful SHA still reconciles current explicit registry/automation drift.
Same VERSION but wrong content/mount cannot produce a success receipt.
No failed/partial attempt replaces a success receipt; no dirty/divergent checkout is overwritten.
Concurrent timer invocations do not overlap writes or sync.
tests: Linux shell integration with disposable Git repos and stub podman; bash -n; Factory suite. Approved live validation uses homelab-ssh and the supported timer/deploy flow, never hand edits.
scope: No promotion changes, new target discovery, service restarts or manual Bazzite checkout edits.
gate: Human approval of this high-risk deployment plan. No hard dependency on #21: retry policy can be implemented and tested independently; release orchestration consumes its receipt later.
